websearch_annotation: "Cities across America are losing children fast. And yet in the country's richest, densest cities, there is one group noticeably defying the trend: wealthier white families." — **Single tweet linking to feature**. **Stance: data-presenting, narrative-affirming with twist.** This is the most recent (May 2026) high-profile mainstream framing of the narrative.

"Two things that are true: 1) Housing is America is too expensive, and we don't build enough, especially in and near our richest densest cities. 2) America is big and very suburban, and the avg US home is also very big by international standards..." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: nuance-presenting / pro-narrative.**

"What's striking is the new study shows that although 'YIMBY for family-friendly units' actually reduces prices by less than 'YIMBY for small apartments,' it actually increases fertility by twice as much. Size matters when it comes to babymaking." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative with housing-type policy implication.**
"Fertility around the country." (map) — **Single tweet with map.** **Stance: data-presenting.**

Yi Fuxian: "While over two-thirds of China's population lives in cities, urban construction occupies just 0.65% of the country's land. The result is exceptionally high population density, which suppresses the fertility rate." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative.**

"There's actually ample evidence that fertility..." (housework / fertility / cities) — **Thread.** **Stance: data-presenting.** ### C. YIMBY camp (housing-supply explanation; kids leaving because we don't build family-sized urban housing)

"Manhattan used to be full of working-class families, and too many have had to move out as housing prices went up. We're going to build 100,000 new homes in the next decade..." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative, YIMBY-flavored.**

"If people can't afford to live in New York City, they can't send their kids to New York City Public Schools. More housing means safer, healthier, and stronger communities." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative.**

"America has a plethora of detached single-family homes in the suburbs and huge 5-over-1 apartment buildings. But we forgot how to build the middle – where middle and upper-middle class families thrived in our cities." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative, missing-middle frame.**
"SMH today reporting that the LGAs where YIMBY v NIMBY fights are happening are hollowing out: less people, less children." — **Quote-tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative, YIMBY.**

"Something that's a little outside my personal experience but that I'm increasingly convinced is imported is there are lots of places in America where the supply of detached single-family homes is unreasonably constrained by lot size rules." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: YIMBY pro-narrative.**

"new paper finds rising housing costs to be a major causal driver of declining fertility. Benjamin Couillard finds higher rents lead to 11 percent fewer US births (~13 million kids) since 1990. That's just over half of the decline in total fertility rate in that time period." — **Single tweet linking to paper.** **Stance: data-presenting, pro-narrative (price channel).**
"'Americans are stuck in place,' reports the WSJ today." — **Single tweet, part of his book "Stuck" promotion.** **Stance: pro-narrative (mobility / opportunity frame).**

"Hell is other people? Not really. Since agriculture humans have gathered in villages, then big cities, & now sprawling (but neighborly) suburbs. But even societies who forget the importance of children don't scatter. We all stay together because the real hell is 'no people'" — **Single tweet.** **Stance: nuance, urbanist defense.** ### D. School-enrollment angle

"Why is enrollment declining in Seattle Public Schools? Reasons pondered in this Seattle Times piece: - low birthrates - migration - 'just fewer kids in Seattle' - high housing costs in Seattle..." — **Thread.** **Stance: data-presenting, skeptical of housing-only explanation.**

"Even some affluent school districts that draw families because of high-performing schools, like in Palo Alto, Calif., and Montclair, N.J., have struggled to maintain enrollment." — **Quote-tweet.** **Stance: data-presenting, expanding narrative to suburbs.**

"House Beautiful: The Cities Young Families Are Flocking to in 2026, According to Real Estate Experts - Carmel, Indiana is on the list!" — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative (families fleeing big metros to smaller ones).**
"Over half of Chicago Public Schools are underutilized, with the city's emptiest public school at just 3% capacity." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative (empty schools as symptom).**

"Steep enrollment declines and inadequate budgeting practices and policies have undermined DC Public Schools' ability to ensure Black and brown students furthest from opportunity get a high-quality education." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: data-presenting.**

"UESF politics and their extremism has done untold damage to SFUSD and has driven the district to bankruptcy. It's questionable whether there should be pay raises when the families of San Francisco can't expect good decisions by their district." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative, blame-progressives.** ### E. Migration / cost-of-living angle

"Young people are leaving Boston and Massachusetts generally, and let's be honest about why: they can't afford to live here. Housing, healthcare, education - the fundamentals of the American dream - are out of reach for the generation we're counting on to build our future." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative.**

"Ballooning housing costs have forced an entire generation of people to make a difficult choice: Stay in Massachusetts, and remain tenants indefinitely, or leave, and put down roots somewhere less expensive." — **Single tweet.** **Stance: pro-narrative.**
